newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sugar joins Midwestern distributing group.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sugar joins Midwestern distributing group.

text.p: U.S. Sugar Corp, one of Florida's largest sugarcane growers, said Tuesday it joined United Sugars Corp, a marketing and distribution alliance made up of three Midwestern sugar beet cooperatives.
The move is expected to increase United Sugars' annual sales to $1.5 billion from $1 billion this year and boost its domestic market share to about 25 percent from 17 percent.
"This positions United Sugars as the first truly national seller of beet and cane sugars," United Sugars President Bob Atwood told a news conference.

United Sugars was formed three years ago by three sugar beet cooperatives -- Southern Minnesota Beet Sugar Cooperative of Moorehead, Minn., Minn-Dak Farmers Cooperative of Wahpeton, N.D., and American Crystal Sugar Co of Renville, Minn.
The addition of the Florida company puts United Sugars on par, in terms of sales and market share, with Domino and Dixie Crystals, the two largest sugar companies in the U.S.
That strengthens United Sugar's position as it gears up for a major advertising and coupon campaign for its newly aquired Pillsbury brand name.

"We have planned for a fight and we are ready," said Dan McCarty, chairman of United Sugars' executive committee. "We like to think that we are bringing aggressive marketing back to the sugar category."
United Sugars recently announced it entered a licensing agreement with Pillsbury, a unit of Grand Metropolitan Plc, to market sugar nationally under the "Pillsbury Best" brand name.
"It really made sense to hook up with a brand name that already had equity in the baking aisle," McCarty said.
The cooperative currently sells about 1.5 tons of refined sugar annnually and packages sugar for more than 200 store brands. About 75 percent of its sales are to food manufacturers.

U.S. Sugar produces about 700,000 tons of raw sugar yearly and expects to begin operations in early 1998 at its first sugar cane refinery, which is under construction near its mill in Clewiston, Fla. It will have an initial annual capacity of 500,000 tons, all of which will be marketed via United Sugar.

The new alliance was expected to boost the competitive strength of U.S. Sugar and United Sugar, but was not expected to have an impact on sugar pricing or the international sugar market, McCarty and U.S. Sugar President Nelson Fairbanks said.

The alliance is the first marriage of sugar beet and sugar cane operations, which are grown in different regions. The two are considered interchangeable in the marketplace, but the alliance is expected to stabilize United Sugar's supplies.
"If you have a bad year in one area it's probably going to be offset in the other," McCarty said.
